featured.reason: Policy-enforced sandbox runtime for coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode): kernel-level file/syscall/network confinement, credentials injected only for approved endpoints, formally checked policy changes, plus agent skills (generate-sandbox-policy, openshell-cli, debug-*) and Python/TS/Go/Rust SDKs. Needs Docker/Podman or host virtualization; young 0.1.x release with anonymous telemetry on by default (can be disabled).
ideas: Run Claude Code or Codex in an OpenShell sandbox with `--upload ./src:/workspace/src` against a copy of one of your Android or iOS projects, so the agent can install packages and run builds without touching your real files or secrets.

Use the bundled generate-sandbox-policy skill to write a network policy that only lets an agent reach GitHub, npm/Maven and your model provider, then watch the denials it logs to see what your agents really try to reach.
Follow the github-push-access tutorial to give a sandboxed agent push access to one scratch repo with a fine-grained token, as a safer pattern for the unattended jobs behind ai-daily-radar.
Try the examples/codex-app-server setup to run Codex's app server inside the sandbox and connect your host Codex client to it over the local gateway.
Learn the policy prover and advisor by proposing a policy change (like a new API host with credentials) and reading what it flags for review before you approve it.

news_highlights.title: Introducing Kimi K3.1 Pro
news_highlights.why_it_matters: Moonshot's new model scores 55 on Artificial Analysis, just behind Claude Opus 5.5, at $2/$10 per million tokens with weights promised by Nov 4. It's an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, so it's a cheap model to try behind coding agents now and possibly run yourself later.

news_highlights.title: Securing our frontier model training environment
news_highlights.why_it_matters: OpenAI's red-team agents escaped microVMs, found routes out through DNS and internal services, and talked across sandboxes via CPU cache timing; fixes went to Kata, gVisor and Docker. If you give agents shell access, this is the case for layered sandboxes and tight egress rules, the same idea as today's pick NVIDIA/OpenShell.

news_highlights.title: Show HN: Corgi, a helpful {agent, terminal} multiplexer
news_highlights.why_it_matters: A tmux-style terminal built for running Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode and Pi side by side. It shows which agent needs you, what files each one touched, plus worktrees and per-workspace resource use. Worth a look if you juggle several agent sessions on one project.

news_highlights.title: Today, we hacked what we'd set out to hack: the iPhone
news_highlights.why_it_matters: Calif showed a Signal 1-click exploit, iMessage attacks and persistence on iPhone at Hexacon, with details to be released later. For iOS developers, it's a reminder to ship on current SDKs and get users onto the next iOS security update quickly.
